submission.natural_language_explanation: In layer 0 the negative pole of N769 is a retrospective current-token dial: it peaks (near its ~0.17 ceiling) on ordinary content words, names, numbers and items like '(' and ',' (e.g. ' must', ' flooded', ' Neil', ' noon', ' prescribed', ' n'), is markedly weaker on high-frequency function words (' the', ' to', ' year', ' not'), and shuts off to ~0 on symbolic operator/markup tokens ('+', '=', '<', '\') and the variable token ' x' where the positive pole spikes instead. It therefore tracks how content-like versus symbol-like the token just read is, and prepares no specific upcoming token (Jacobian and logit lens top-10 lists agree on 0 tokens, kurtosis ~3.0).
